transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-02 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 56m
- Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Luca Romano (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ko (BlueHarbor), Maya Lin (BlueHarbor SRE), Carlos Ortega (BlueHarbor VP Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): brief recap of throttle spiral where concurrent requests caused per-tenant throttles to cascade; short-term fix: stricter front-door rate limits + temporary model degradation path.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everybody, thanks for carving time. Luca, you want to kick off with the customer context?
[00:12] Luca Romano: Yeah, thanks. Quick high level: BlueHarbor saw a spike last week where many smaller shipments triggered heavy NLU scoring, and then the throughput dropped because of throttles at the inference gateway and then the dedicated pools sort of backed up, right.
[00:28] Daniel Ko: Yeah that's right. It looked like a feedback loop — the front door started rejecting, clients retried, and that drove more connections into the low-level backends. We hit our burst cap on dedicated and then the K-V cache warmed up wrong, I think.
[00:46] Maya Lin: sorry, I said K-V cash earlier in the ticket but it's the KV cache. Some of the caches had a stale eviction pattern so the cache wasn't being hit which forced more full model runs.
[01:03] Priya Shah: Right, and from our side we saw a high number of cache-miss amplified requests with small sequence lengths which made the kernel scheduler jump contexts. The runtime started throttling per-tenant to protect other customers.
[01:20] Carlos Ortega: We were on a tight window because our SLAs are tight. The initial mitigation you gave was helpful but we're still nervous about the long-tail timeouts.
[01:34] Jordan Miles: Understood. Today's goal: align on owners for short-term guardrails, confirm what Redwood will deliver this week, and agree on a verification plan.
[01:46] Daniel Ko: Quick question — was there any sign the model itself regressed? Or was it purely infrastructure?
[01:52] Priya Shah: From our traces it's infrastructure-heavy. There was a small uptick in tokenization time for corner cases but not at the magnitude to explain the cascade. The dominant signal was concurrent open connections + cache misses.
[02:10] Maya Lin: We also found a misconfigured client-side retry — exponential backoff wasn't set properly, so retries were too aggressive. That's on our side to fix.
[02:22] Carlos Ortega: ok fair.
[02:29] Jordan Miles: Let's go through specific mitigations. Priya, can you outline what we can push fast?
[02:33] Priya Shah: Sure. Short-term (hours): 1) tighten front-door per-tenant rate limits and add a soft-queue with 429+Retry-After, 2) enable prefix/KV caching for the hot paths, 3) temporary downgrade to a lighter quantized model for non-critical routes so less GPU time per request. We'll provide the autoscale patch and suggested SLOs.
[02:56] Daniel Ko: That downgrade — is it an automatic fallback or manual? We need it to be predictable.
[03:03] Priya Shah: We can do both. Option A: automatic policy when backend latency exceeds threshold; Option B: manual triggered button. For this week we recommend manual to avoid surprises.
[03:15] Maya Lin: Manual is fine, but can you provide a one-click runbook so our on-call can flip it?
[03:20] Priya Shah: Yep, we'll give a runbook and the jackson — sorry, the dashboard toggle.
[03:26] Jordan Miles: (chuckles) jackson toggle — dashboard toggle.
[03:29] Luca Romano: We'll also share a sanitized status note draft for your customers.
[03:33] Carlos Ortega: Great.
[03:38] [05:00] Jordan Miles: (later in call) On the KV cache sanity checks — Maya, you mentioned a dump. What format do you need from us?
[05:10] Maya Lin: Ideally we get a key-sample dump with timestamps and eviction counters. I know that's a lot, but even a small sample will help. The scripts you sent didn't capture eviction counters last time.
[05:25] Priya Shah: We'll update the dump script. We may have mis-labeled some labels in the previous run, that's likely why counters were missing — transcription note: labels sometimes show as K-V-cash in the ticket.
[05:40] Daniel Ko: On auditing: are there any PII retention concerns if we enable debug sampling?
[05:47] Jordan Miles: Good point. We can limit debug sampling to metadata only and scrub tokens. Redwood's debug pipeline has scrubbing hooks; we can run it through customer-managed KMS if needed.
[05:59] Carlos Ortega: We need confirmation in writing for legal.
[06:02] Luca Romano: I'll attach the data handling note.
[06:08] [10:12] Maya Lin: Something I spotted — the routing policy fell through when a single AZ lost connectivity, requests were funneled into the remaining nodes with no regional-shard awareness. Can Redwood set a shard-aware fallback to avoid overloading a single pool?
[10:25] Priya Shah: Yes, we have a shard-aware policy, but your config had regional fallback turned off when we onboarded your dedicated capacity because of a constraint on data residency. There's a tradeoff — turning it on improves resilience but might replicate minimal state cross-region.
[10:42] Daniel Ko: What's the replication cost?
[10:45] Priya Shah: It's small — metadata only. We won't replicate customer data payloads.
[10:50] Jordan Miles: We'll draft a table with tradeoffs and costs.
[11:00] [15:00] Carlos Ortega: On the longer-term fixes — what are the top three?
[15:07] Priya Shah: 1) better autoscaling heuristics by workload shape, 2) KV cache eviction policy improvements and per-tenant quotas on cache usage, 3) smarter retry guidance for clients (exponential backoff + jitter).
[15:22] Maya Lin: For autoscaling, can you provide simulated load tests? The last perf run didn't match production distributions.
[15:29] Priya Shah: We will — sending a micro-benchmark and a synthetic trace generator. It will include sequence-length distributions.
[15:35] Daniel Ko: We'll run it in our staging and report back.
[15:40] [20:01] Jordan Miles: Ok, let's capture owners. Luca: customer comms. Priya: autoscale config and runbook. Maya: KV dump and the on-call note. Luca: you'll send the status note.
[20:12] Luca Romano: noted.
[20:15] [25:00] Daniel Ko: Another question — does Redwood keep a rolling audit log for throttles and policy changes? We need that for our compliance teams.
[25:09] Jordan Miles: Yes, we have audit logs. We'll enable extended retention for your account and share access patterns; there may be a cost delta.
[25:20] Carlos Ortega: fine, please share numbers.
[25:24] [30:02] Maya Lin: FYI we discovered a client misbehaving — a 3rd party worker was hammering the API due to a bug. We're patching that, but can Redwood filter excessive traffic with a stricter per-client token bucket?
[30:18] Priya Shah: We can add a per-client token-bucket layer at the gateway, yes. That would reduce blast radius quickly.
[30:25] Daniel Ko: Great.
[30:30] [35:00] Priya Shah: One more note — when you enable prefix cache there can be edge cases where similar prompts diverge and cache hit rate drops. We'll provide heuristics for prompt normalization.
[35:15] Maya Lin: Please include examples.
[35:18] Priya Shah: Will do.
[35:22] [40:00] Jordan Miles: Any blockers on legal/PII for debug sampling?
[40:06] Carlos Ortega: Legal wants the scrubbed pipeline and the KMS flow documented.
[40:12] Luca Romano: We'll add that to the package.
[40:18] [45:00] Jordan Miles: Recap of what Redwood will deliver this week: autoscale patch, dashboard toggle runbook, updated KV dump script, sanitized status note, and micro-benchmark sheet.
[45:13] Priya Shah: And sample scripts for prefix normalization.
[45:17] Luca Romano: I'll draft the customer-facing comms after receiving your KV dump.
[45:22] [50:00] Daniel Ko: For the follow-up, let's aim next Tuesday at 15:00 UTC.
[50:06] Jordan Miles: Sounds good, we'll send invite.
[50:10] Maya Lin: thanks everyone.
[50:12] Carlos Ortega: appreciate the fast response.
[50:15] Jordan Miles: Thanks all — action owners noted, we'll sync early.

Call close.
